title: Straight Lines
summary: The slope of a line making angle θ with the positive x-axis is m = tan θ. A line parallel to the x-axis has slope 0. Parallel lines have equal slopes; perpendicular lines have m₁m₂ = −1. A line making 60° with the negative x-axis makes 120° with the positive x-axis, so its slope is tan 120° = −√3.

Slope–intercept: y = mx + c. Point–slope: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Two-point: y − y₁ = [(y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)](x − x₁). Intercept form: x/a + y/b = 1. Normal form: x cos α + y sin α = p. General form: Ax + By + C = 0, with slope −A/B, x-intercept −C/A and y-intercept −C/B.
A line cutting equal intercepts has equation x + y = a, so its slope is −1.
The perpendicular distance of (x₁, y₁) from Ax + By + C = 0 is |Ax₁ + By₁ + C|/√(A² + B²). The distance between parallel lines Ax + By + C₁ = 0 and Ax + By + C₂ = 0 is |C₁ − C₂|/√(A² + B²).
A line through the intersection of L₁ = 0 and L₂ = 0 has the form L₁ + λL₂ = 0, or find the point of intersection first and use the point–slope form.
The foot of the perpendicular from (x₁, y₁) to Ax + By + C = 0 is given by (x − x₁)/A = (y − y₁)/B = −(Ax₁ + By₁ + C)/(A² + B²).

objective: (a) The slope of the line y + 3 = 0 is ______. (b) The slope of the line through (2, 5) and (4, 9) is ______.

(a) y = −3 is parallel to the x-axis ⇒ slope 0.
(b) (9 − 5)/(4 − 2) = 2.
Fill in the blanks: (a) The line through (1, −2) cutting equal intercepts on the axes is ______. (b) Two lines are perpendicular if m₁m₂ = ______.

(a) x + y = a passes through (1, −2) ⇒ a = −1 ⇒ x + y + 1 = 0.
(b) −1
